editorial:
Imagine being eleven years old and deciding to track down a father you barely know just to say goodbye. That is the heavy setup here. You get to follow this young boy as he spends a short, awkward amount of time with his dad, who is clearly struggling with his own life. The vibe is very raw and honest. It does not try to pretend that everything will be okay with a magic hug. Instead, you see a really tense and sometimes inappropriate relationship where both people are trying to figure out how to talk to each other without breaking down.

What really makes this work is the acting, which feels totally natural and not like a scripted movie. You will feel the tension in every scene, though some parts might feel a bit slow if you are looking for a big plot. It is a quiet movie, but it hits hard. If you enjoy stories about family secrets and emotional growth, you should definitely give this a shot. You can rent it on Apple TV for a quick watch, or if you want the best picture, try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to catch all the small details in the actors faces.
endingExplained: The movie ends with the boy finally leaving his father after their short visit. There is no big happy reunion or a promise that they will be a normal family again. Instead, they reach a quiet understanding of who they are. You see that while they cannot fix the past, the boy has found some closure. He walks away knowing the truth about his dad, leaving their relationship in a sad but honest place.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves realistic stories about family and forgiveness.
